evidence.title: Vicente Aranda
evidence.text: Vicente Aranda Ezquerra (9 November 1926 – 26 May 2015) was a Spanish film director, screenwriter and producer.

evidence.title: Vicente Aranda
evidence.text: Due to his refined and personal style, he was one of the most renowned Spanish filmmakers.

evidence.title: Vicente Aranda
evidence.text: He started as a founding member of the Barcelona School of Film and became known for bringing contemporary Spanish novels to life on the big screen.

evidence.title: Vicente Aranda
evidence.text: Aranda was also noted for exploring difficult social issues and variations on the theme of desire while using the codes of melodrama.

evidence.title: Vicente Aranda
evidence.text: Love as uncontrollable passion, eroticism and cruelty are constant themes in his filmography.

evidence.title: Vicente Aranda
evidence.text: The frank examination of sexuality is one of the trademarks of his work, as seen in his most internationally successful film: "Amantes" (1990) "(Lovers)".

evidence.title: Sjumandjaja
evidence.text: Sjumandjaja( Perfected Spelling: Syumanjaya; 5 August 1934 – 19 July 1985) was an Indonesian director, screenwriter, and actor.

evidence.title: Sjumandjaja
evidence.text: During his career he wrote numerous films, directed fourteen, acted in ten, and produced nine; he also won five Citra Awards from the Indonesian Film Festival.

evidence.title: Sjumandjaja
evidence.text: His films reflected social realism.

evidence.title: Sjumandjaja
evidence.text: Sjumandjaja was born in Batavia( modern day Jakarta), Dutch East Indies, and grew up there.

evidence.title: Sjumandjaja
evidence.text: During high school, he became interested in creative writing and acting, eventually joining the Senen Artists' Group.

evidence.title: Sjumandjaja
evidence.text: In 1956, when one of his short stories was adapted into a film, Sjumandjaja became active in the filmmaking industry, writing two films for the production company Persari.

evidence.title: Sjumandjaja
evidence.text: After receiving a government scholarship, he moved to Moscow and attended the All- Union State Institute of Cinematography.

evidence.title: Sjumandjaja
evidence.text: Upon returning to Indonesia in 1965, Sjumandjaja took a job at the Ministry of Information and continued writing screenplays.

evidence.title: Sjumandjaja
evidence.text: In 1971, after leaving the ministry, he directed his first feature film," Lewat Tengah MalamPast Midnight").

evidence.title: Sjumandjaja
evidence.text: He continued to write and direct films until his death from a heart attack on 19 July 1985.

evidence.title: Sjumandjaja
evidence.text: Reportedly a strict director, Sjumandjaja valued creative value over receiving a director's fee.

evidence.title: Sjumandjaja
evidence.text: He married three times and had three children, two with his first wife and one with his second.

evidence.title: Sjumandjaja
evidence.text: His son, Sri Aksana, is the former drummer of Dewa 19, and his daughter Djenar Maesa Ayu is also a Citra Award- winning director.
